authorization: Operator conditional Phase 3 authorization: coalescer implementation and local validation only; no host restart, commit, release, DNA change, queue operation, or mission transition.
symptom: Repeated-looking Behavior-OS notices appeared in a burst and historical notices arrived long after the decisions they described.

rootCause.classification: late FIFO drain of distinct historical notices, not duplicate delivery
evidence: 19 synthetic deliveries carried 19 distinct message IDs; zero duplicate IDs.
14 notices drained between 12:00:11Z and 12:03:01Z (170 s); the other 5 were delivered earlier.
session_inbox was empty at 12:09:32Z; the last rejection was 11:56:20Z; no synthetic delivery occurred after 12:03:01Z.

The host inbox schema has no acknowledgement, attempt, cursor, dedupe or expiry columns. Delivery is acknowledged implicitly by deleting the row after it is materialised into session_message with the same ID and a new sequence/time.
The plugin producer emitted one notice per deny, escalate, DNA selection and mission creation with delivery=queue and no coalescing or staleness metadata.

Representative IDs: msg_158e62637001ooIrt97ZUf87sE (sequence 1348, produced 10:40:40Z, delivered 12:02:44Z) and msg_1592bb4330010G1mzcjvGW2FKF (sequence 3433, produced 11:56:38Z, delivered 12:03:01Z).

identityKey: reason normalized by collapsing whitespace and trimming
fix.normalization: Whitespace only. Case, punctuation and wording are preserved so distinct decisions never share a key.
fix.resetSemantics: Only the session.prompt hook resets a window. OpenCode does not run that hook for synthetic messages, so a notice cannot re-enable itself. The hook runs before admission, so a prompt that fails preparation reopens the window early; this errs toward more notices, never fewer.
fix.persistence: Versioned snapshot under ctx.storage key behavioros:notifications:v1. take() is synchronous, so the duplicate check, cap check and record cannot interleave within one runtime. Snapshot writes are serialized so an older snapshot cannot overwrite a newer one.
fix.delivery: delivery=queue is unchanged; notices never interrupt a turn.
fix.observability: Each suppression appends one advisory governance-log entry with the suppression reason and aggregate counters. It never emits another synthetic message.

notImplemented: deletion or replay of host inbox records
hostBoundary.reason: These live in the OpenCode host consumer, not in this repository. The coalescer reduces producer redundancy and does not claim timely delivery.

focused.command: pnpm --filter @behavior-os/opencode-plugin exec vitest run tests/notifications.test.ts tests/plugin-registration.test.ts

coveredRegressions: identical identity inside the window is suppressed
distinct action, kind, reason or session is not suppressed
whitespace normalization does not merge different case or punctuation
per-session cap and recovery after the window
reset clears the window and returns counters
snapshot/restore continues suppression and respects expiry
deep-copied snapshot cannot mutate live state
invalid snapshots are rejected without changing live state
many callers in one turn produce exactly one send
transport rejection does not crash or retry the blocked operation
metadata carries kind, key, time and suppression counters
governance log remains append-only and retains every deny decision
mission version, status and timestamps are unchanged by coalescing
restart restores the window and a real prompt reopens it

preserved.docs/analysis/governance-conformance.jso: Pre-existing working-tree change preserved byte-for-byte. SHA-256 221748E18F75E39C0ADBAB87569A31C70E4275B01FC2BC8061AAFC8EE016F25F. The file was backed up before the governance gate regenerated it and restored afterwards.

residualRisks: Host-side lateness remains: the coalescer does not acknowledge, expire or prioritise inbox records (C11).
Cross-process dedupe is not guaranteed: ctx.storage has no compare-and-swap, so two plugin instances sharing one session could each admit one notice. Within one process, take() is atomic.
If session.synthetic rejects, the key is already recorded. The governance decision remains in the log, but the on-screen notice may be lost for that window.
The window is wall-clock based; a clock jump can extend it.
The live host still runs the previous plugin build. The change is not active until a separately authorised restart.
pnpm audit --audit-level=high still fails (G-016) and remains an unrelated release blocker.
